Canvas: 1080×1350px square carousel, 3 slides minimum (white or soft cream background to anchor green hierarchy).

Slide 1 (Hook/Education):
- Background: clean cream (#f5f1ed or similar warm white) with no competing pattern.
- Headline (Satoshi Bold, ~95–110px, hierarchy-dominant): Approximately 12–14 words introducing the physiological shift. Centre-align above the graph. Use ONE meaningful word (e.g., "progesterone" or "decline") in green #39B54A italic bold to anchor the visual. Remainder in dark charcoal (#2c2c2c).
- Central graphic: a simplified, grounded two-line chart showing progesterone and estradiol across life stages (childhood, reproductive years, perimenopause, postmenopause). Progesterone line (solid, muted sage green #6b8e7f or soft teal) shows steeper early decline. Estradiol line (muted rose or warm grey-brown #a89080) tracks separately. Label the perimenopause phase with a soft green box (#39B54A at 30% opacity) behind or highlighting the transition zone. No busy axis labels—only the stage names (small, charcoal, Satoshi Medium 14–18px). The graph occupies the centre 60–70% of the card width, breathing room on left/right.
- Credit/source line: bottom right, light grey (#999999), Satoshi Medium 12px, e.g., "Educational reference based on endocrine literature."

Slide 2 (Validation/Symptoms):
- Background: same cream.
- Headline: ~80px, Satoshi Bold, centred. Four to six words emphasising what this means for the body. One word in green #39B54A italic.
- Body: three short stacked callouts (Satoshi Medium, 40–44px), each on its own line. Examples:
  • "Progesterone drops first 🔥 [Anti-inflammatory support]"
  • "Anxiety & sleep shift 😔 [The mood-regulating hormone]"
  • "Histamine rises ⬆️ [Progesterone helps regulate it]"
  Use emoji sparingly (one per line, right-aligned). Keep text left-aligned, generous left margin (~80px). Green #39B54A as a light vertical rule or accent bar (10–15px wide) down the left edge, behind the text.
- Whitespace: 40–60px padding top/bottom.

Slide 3 (Reframe/Functional Lens):
- Background: same cream.
- Headline: ~70–80px, Satoshi Bold, centred. Six to eight words offering a functional-medicine perspective. One word in green #39B54A italic.
- Body: two to three sentences (Satoshi Medium, 40px line-height, charcoal), centred, ~60–70% max-width to preserve breathing room. E.g., "This isn't a deficiency—it's a transition. Recognising what's shifting helps us support your body with targeted nutrition, sleep and stress strategies."
- CTA line (subtle): "Let's work out what matters most for you. Book a consultation." Satoshi Medium, 36px, charcoal, with a soft green underline or bullet (green #39B54A, 4–6px stroke).
- Footer: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in Satoshi Bold, 24–28px, green #39B54A, centred, with a tiny logo lockup (unobtrusive, <20px) to the left.

Overall feel: Clinical, warm, and intentionally spaced. Green #39B54A is the visual anchor (headline accent, left rule, footer text, graph highlight box). Secondary palette (sage teal, muted rose-brown, charcoal, cream) harmonises with green. No competitor's exact hex values, no pure black backgrounds, no serif fonts. Satoshi throughout. Legibility enforced: no text under 36px (body), headlines 70–110px depending on line count. Copy shortened to fit the grid; never shrunk.

posts.caption:
Perimenopause doesn't start with missed periods—it starts with progesterone. For many women, the first changes are mood, sleep and energy shifts that happen months or years before your cycle skips a beat.

Progesterone is your anti-inflammatory, anti-anxiety, histamine-regulating hormone. When it drops (which happens first in the perimenopause transition), you *feel* it.

This is why tracking your symptoms—not just your calendar—matters so much. Understanding what's actually shifting helps us build a plan that works *for your body*, not against it.

If you're noticing changes in mood, sleep, anxiety or unexplained inflammation, let's have a chat about what's happening and what support might help.

Book a consultation to get started.

posts.caption:
When we talk about emotional resilience, we often focus on therapy or mindset. But neuroscience tells us something quieter: sleep is where your brain recalibrates emotional regulation. Poor sleep doesn't just make you tired — it quietly erodes your ability to manage stress and process difficult feelings.

In functional medicine, we see this pattern all the time. When we support sleep quality (via sleep hygiene, addressing deficiencies, and calming nervous-system load), our patients often report surprising shifts in mood and emotional clarity. It's not because we're treating a "mental illness" — it's because we're restoring a foundational system.

If you're noticing you're more reactive, anxious, or flat lately, sleep might be the missing piece. Worth investigating.

Ready to explore what's driving your sleep and mood? Let's talk.

Format: Vertical reel cover (9:16), single full-frame image. NO palm trees — replace with eucalyptus or native Australian foliage to ground locally. Subject stands naturally, conveying warmth and clinical authority.

Background treatment: Dappled natural daylight, soft focus behind subject. A subtle coloured overlay or border accent in EHN green (#39B54A) — perhaps a thin vertical or horizontal line, or a soft semi-transparent wash — anchors green as the primary visual anchor without dominating. Secondary palette: sage, cream, soft grey-blue undertones in the foliage; charcoal for body text if needed. NEVER pure black background, never the competitor's tropical palette.

Text hierarchy: Headline dominates (white/charcoal + green accent word). No secondary text on-frame except brand/close line. Clean whitespace around headline allows text to breathe and remain legible at 36px minimum on mobile.

Logo/branding: Small, unobtrusive EHN logo lockup (white or charcoal) in top-right corner, ~2–3% of canvas width. Close line "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in green (#39B54A) at bottom centre, Satoshi Medium, ~48–52px, ensuring clarity.

Overall feel: Grounded, editorial, clinical-but-warm. Australian natural light and foliage. High contrast headline + soft background = strong CTA pull. Conversational intrigue (question format) invites tap-to-discover without hyperbole.
